children: DayOne Data Centers Limited filed for an initial public offering of American Depositary Shares on the Nasdaq under the ticker DODC. The Singapore-headquartered company builds and operates hyperscale data center campuses, primarily serving global cloud and AI customers outside the U.S. and China. Prior to this offering, there has been no public market for its ADSs.

DayOne Data Centers develops, owns and operates hyperscale data center campuses for global cloud and technology companies. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Singapore, the company focuses on high-growth regions outside the U.S. and China, delivering large-scale, high-specification capacity with an industrialized, modular approach designed for speed, reliability and cost efficiency.

DayOne’s platform spans Asia Pacific and Europe, with flagship development in the SIJORI region (Singapore, Johor, Batam). It serves AI training and inference, public cloud and enterprise workloads through long-term, largely take‑or‑pay contracts. The company emphasizes standardized engineering, prefabrication, and strong utility and government engagement to secure powered land and accelerate time‑to‑market. Customers are primarily global hyperscalers, and the company highlights cost advantages, rapid delivery, and multi‑market execution as core competitive strengths.
: Global installed data center capacity projected to grow from 90 GW (2025) to 225 GW (2030)
: AI expected to drive ~59% of incremental demand; APAC (ex-China) to grow from 16 GW to 49 GW and Europe from 16 GW to 38 GW (2025–2030)
: ~33% SIJORI market share by bookings; early mover building multi-gigawatt campuses
: Other hyperscale-focused colocation developers in APAC and Europe
: Supply constraints in established hubs, shift to growth markets, rising outsourcing penetration, acceleration of AI training and inference workloads
: Seven global hyperscale and leading technology customers; three engage for multi‑market deployments around or exceeding 200 MW each

: Multi‑gigawatt campuses across SIJORI (Singapore, Johor, Batam), Greater Bangkok (Thailand), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), Greater Helsinki (Finland), Zaragoza (Spain), Kyushu and Tokyo (Japan), and Hong Kong
: 10 markets with 4.6 GW of Resources secured since inception
: Strategic collaboration with a sovereign wealth fund in Indonesia (Batam) and long‑term utility and government engagement for powered land
: Approximately 2.3 GW of Bookings expected to be delivered substantially by year‑end 2028

: 962 MW Capacity In Service, 953 MW Billings, 1.328 GW Backlog, ~99% Utilization Rate, ~99% Pre‑Commitment Rate (as of Sept 20, 2026); 2.3 GW Secured Powered Land and 1.3 GW Powered Land Pipeline; estimated ~$11.4B cost to complete current Bookings; ~33% market share in SIJORI by bookings
, Chief Executive Officer and Director - 30+ years in finance and digital infrastructure; former COO/Deputy CFO at GDS; previously with ST Telemedia, ABB, EY, and Baker Hughes.
, Chairman of the Board - Veteran executive and director across Asian corporates; former Chairman of Olam Group; ex‑Chairman of Morgan Grenfell (Asia).
, Director - Chairman and CEO of GDS; two decades in data center industry leadership and growth.
, Director - Senior executive roles across SoftBank and Alibaba Japan; 20+ years in global tech and digital infrastructure.
, Director - Former CEO of HKEX; ex‑CEO roles at J.P. Morgan in APAC and Private Bank; director at MercadoLibre and Globant.
, Director - Partner at Achi Capital; former CEO and head of global sales at VIA China; engineering background (UC Berkeley).
, Director - Founder of Quintet Partners; former Deputy CEO at Vinhomes; ex‑Head of M&A and Real Estate IB (ANZ) at Citigroup.
, Director (upon effectiveness) - Vice Chairman at Nasdaq; 20 years building Nasdaq listings franchises across APAC and Latin America.
, Chief Financial Officer - Former investor at Hillhouse and KKR; earlier investment banking at Citi; SMU business graduate.
, Chief Legal Officer - Former partner at Simpson Thacher; 24 years in capital markets advisory and execution.
: Morgan Stanley; J.P. Morgan; BofA Securities; Citigroup; BNP Paribas
: Development and construction of new data center projects; working capital and other general corporate purposes
